name: sprintly
description: Drive the sprintly CLI for sprintly.cloud task tracking. LLM-agnostic mirror of SKILL.md.

auth.headless_trigger: missing DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY auto-selects the code-pairing prompt
auth.logout_warning: Run only when the user explicitly asks; revokes the saved session.
auth.session_path_note: ~/.sprintly/ holds only the installed binary and shell completions — no credentials there.
auth.token_for_rest: `sprintly token` refreshes the session and prints a valid access token on stdout (one line, nothing else; diagnostics go to stderr). Use it for REST calls the CLI does not cover: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(sprintly token)". Never read accessToken out of config.json by hand — tokens live ~5 minutes, so a hand-read value is often already expired and the 401 surfaces as a parse error.

lookups.returns: custom field definitions and value sets; the full dictionary is admin-only, otherwise the command explains that on stderr and falls back to deriving fields from values present on issues (POSSIBLE VALUES = values in use, not the allowed set; FORMAT/REQ unknown)
member IDs and names of one project; works without admin rights (reads project memberships)

output_format.available_on: every command that prints data: projects, statuses, priorities, types, activities, sprints, custom-fields, users, issue create|update|show|list, wiki list|show|edit, attachment download
output_format.shape: Collection -> JSON array; single resource -> JSON object. No envelope, so .[] iterates a list.
output_format.keys: camelCase, named after the CLI flag vocabulary (type, sprint, assignee, doneRatio, customFields) rather than the wire format of the API underneath. This is the CLI contract, so it is stable across backend renames.
output_format.prefer_when: Always prefer --json over parsing tables when you are going to act on the values.
output_format.write_commands: issue create --json prints the created issue (read .id); issue update --json and wiki edit --json print a confirmation object, because those calls return no body. attachment upload --json is the one envelope: {"issue","count","uploaded":[{"id","filename","filesize","contentType"}]} — read new attachment ids from .uploaded[].id.
output_format.table_cells: Table output collapses line breaks inside a cell to spaces, and cuts the free-text columns (description, cf:<id>) at 120 characters with a trailing "…". Reference-data tables are never truncated. Both are display concessions — read values you intend to use via --json or issue show --field.

single_field.purpose: Print one field value on stdout with no labels, padding or terminator — the read half of a read-modify-write loop over a text field.
single_field.names: Same names as `issue list --columns` (id, subject, description, project, type, status, priority, author, assignee, category, sprint, parent, start-date, due-date, done-ratio, estimated-hours, is-private, created, updated, cf:<id>) plus comments and attachments.
single_field.plain_semantics: Strings print without quotes; an unset field prints nothing; objects and arrays print as compact JSON.
single_field.raw_flag: --raw drops the trailing newline so stdout equals the value byte for byte. Requires --field; on its own it is an error.
single_field.json_flag: With --json the same single value is printed as a typed JSON value.

output_format.comment_metadata: Comment bodies come back clean: the CLI strips the internal <!--jmeta:{...}--> prefix the web client stores inside journal notes, and hides entries the metadata marks as deleted. Do not handle that prefix yourself.

issue show.purpose: Show full detail for one issue. When the issue has attachments, an Attachments block lists each one's ID, filename, size, type, author and date; use the ID with `attachment download`.

flags.--comments: Also list the issue comments (journal notes): author, timestamp, optional [private] marker, note body. Field-change-only history entries are omitted.
flags.--json: Emit the issue as a JSON object instead of the pretty-printed block (see output_format)
flags.--field: Print only this field's value on stdout, with no labels or padding (see output_format.single_field)
flags.--raw: With --field: omit the trailing newline so stdout equals the value byte for byte

attachment upload.purpose: Attach one or more local files to an issue — the only supported way to get a file INTO the tracker. Wraps the REST two-step (POST /api/uploads, then PUT /api/issues/<id> with an uploads array). All --file arguments land in ONE journal entry. The stored filename is computed once and reused for both steps: the backend verifies it on download, so a mismatch would surface as a 404 later rather than an error at upload time.

flags.--file: File to attach; repeatable. A missing path is reported before any network call.
flags.--content-type: Content type applied to every --file; guessed from the extension by default.
flags.--notes: Comment posted together with the files. Primitive HTML, same rule as --description.
flags.--filename: Store under a different name; an error when combined with more than one --file.

attachment upload.returns: After upload the issue is re-read and the new attachment IDs are printed — those are the IDs `attachment download` expects.

attachment download.purpose: Download the bytes of an issue attachment (e.g. a screenshot). Fetches metadata first, so it works from just the ID. With no --output, writes to the attachment's original filename in the current directory.

flags.--output: Destination path; -o is the short form, and -o - streams the bytes to stdout

issue list.purpose: Search and list issues with rich filtering.

flags.--columns: Comma-separated columns; cf:<id> adds a custom-field column

issue list.example: sprintly issue list --assignee me --status open --sort updated_on:desc

issue create.json_semantics: JSON provides the base body; CLI flags override individual fields.

flags.--assignee: ID | me | NAME. NAME is matched against project members: exact case-insensitive match first, then substring; zero or multiple matches are an error that lists the members. Note `issue list --assignee` takes ID|me only.

gotchas: A project may have required custom fields; omitting one fails with HTTP 422 (e.g. 'Release version cannot be blank' on spr, CF 67). Check custom-fields --project <ID> first.
--json prints the created issue as a flat object (no envelope): read .id directly.

issue update.purpose: Update an existing issue and/or append a journal comment.

extra_flags.--notes: Append a journal comment without otherwise mutating the issue
extra_flags.--private-notes: Mark the appended comment as private

flags.--assignee: ID | me | NAME. NAME is matched against project members: exact case-insensitive match first, then substring; zero or multiple matches are an error that lists the members. Note `issue list --assignee` takes ID|me only.

users.purpose: List backend users with substring / status / group filters, pagination, and selectable columns. Used to look up a numeric user id when `me` does not apply (e.g. for --watcher).

flags.--project: List members of one project instead of every account. Works WITHOUT admin rights; returns IDs and names only (--status/--group/--include do not apply). This is how to resolve a person to a numeric id when plain `users` answers 403.
flags.--hide-admin: Client-side filter on the admin field. Backend only returns admin to admin callers; for regular users this filter is a no-op.
flags.--all: Fetch every page until total_count is reached.
flags.--columns: Comma-separated columns. Available: id,login,name,email,last-login,admin. Default: id,login,name,email,last-login.

wiki list.purpose: List wiki pages of one project.

flags.--project: Numeric project ID or project identifier (slug from `sprintly projects`)

wiki list.notes: Pagination is client-side; the wiki index endpoint does not return total_count, so there is no --all flag.

wiki show.purpose: Show a wiki page by title.

flags.--project: Numeric project ID or project identifier
flags.--title: Page name. The backend addresses wiki pages by title only; numeric IDs are not supported.
flags.--format: raw|rendered. 'rendered' is a forward-compat placeholder and currently behaves like 'raw'.

wiki show.errors: Missing title returns a clear not-found error via describeBackendError; spaces in title are URL-encoded automatically.

wiki edit.purpose: Upsert a wiki page by title — one command for both create and update.

flags.--project: Numeric project ID or project identifier
flags.--title: Page name (primary key for wiki pages)
flags.--text: Inline body. Mutually exclusive with --text-file and --text-stdin.
flags.--text-file: Read body from file. Mutually exclusive with --text and --text-stdin.
flags.--text-stdin: Read body from stdin. Mutually exclusive with --text and --text-file.
flags.--parent: Parent page title (sets parent_title on the page)
flags.--comments: Revision note attached to this edit

wiki edit.notes: PUT without text is valid when you only want to change --parent or attach --comments to an existing page. Body follows the same primitive-HTML rule as --description/--notes.
wiki edit.example:
sprintly wiki edit --project spr --title 'Release notes' --text '

Shipped #54.

' --comments 'ship note'

text_format.rule: Human-readable text wrapped in primitive HTML tags. Plain unmarked text and Markdown are both wrong: Markdown (**bold**, # heading, backticks, - list) renders as raw syntax in the web UI.

story_workflow.rule: When implementing a story that has sub-tasks, keep the sprintly tracker in sync at all times. The in-session task list is invisible to the user later; only journal notes and statuses on sub-tasks survive.

per_sub_task.action: Transition to in progress (status 2; verify with `sprintly statuses`).
If you hit a blocker, scope change, or split a sub-task, leave a --notes entry explaining why. Do not rely on memory or the in-session task list.
Transition to Done (status 3) AND post a short --notes summary: files/functions touched, decisions made, verification results. Do not paste diffs.
per_sub_task.example:
sprintly issue update --id 41 --status 3 --notes "

Added User in Cli.Backend; admin is Maybe Bool so the client-side filter degrades cleanly.

"

story_workflow.parent_story: When the story itself is finished, post a summary note on the parent issue, but do not auto-transition the parent unless the user explicitly asks. Let them choose review/testing/done.
story_workflow.why: The sprintly journal is the only artefact the user can read tomorrow to understand what shipped and why. Skipping it leaves the board lying — sub-tasks stuck in `to do` while their code is merged.

known_gaps.summary: There is no issue delete command.
known_gaps.workaround: Close the issue by setting --status to the Done ID from `sprintly statuses`.

known_gaps.summary: `attachment download --json` cannot be combined with `--output -`: both would write to stdout.
known_gaps.workaround: Write the file to a path and read the JSON report, or stream to stdout without --json.
Use `issue update --id N --notes "…"`, or `attachment upload --notes "…"` when a file goes with it.

known_gaps.summary: There is no attachment delete command.
The full custom-field dictionary and the global user list are admin-only.
known_gaps.workaround: `custom-fields` falls back to fields seen on issues; use `users --project ID` instead of plain `users`.
